clue.text: Floor stones

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to baffle or flummox someone completely
second meaning: small loose pebbles, as on a path or drive

explanation.surface: A floor made of stones, like a cobbled courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor' reads as a noun, but here it is the verb meaning to stump someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor a person is to puzzle them utterly, and loose small pebbles laid on paths share the same word.

clue.text: Minder set about the lady's daughter

parts.note: to set about someone is to go at them
her is the possessive for a woman
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A minder attacks a woman's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set about' splits as GO AT. The minder is not a bodyguard but someone minding animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatherd is a person who looks after a flock of goats, a minder of livestock.

clue.text: Loving trouble and a place to fight

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
a boxing or wrestling ring

explanation.surface: Affection, then strife, and somewhere to have it out: a stormy romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring means showing deep love and devotion towards someone, the warmest form of affection.

clue.text: One looking out for outdated coins, Crown property by right

parts.note: ex means former or no longer current
treasure trove, buried coins whose owner is unknown, belonged to the Crown
RT is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A collector searching for old coins that by law belong to the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One looking out for' reads as a searcher, but the definition is just 'One looking out', someone turned outwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An extrovert is an outgoing person whose attention is directed outward to other people and the world.

clue.text: String is kept here-hang a label inside

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece sits within the letters of the other

parts.note: to sling something is to hang or suspend it
a tab is a small label attached to something

explanation.surface: Somewhere string is stored, with a label hung up inside to mark it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'String' is not twine but a racing string, the horses kept by one trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer's string of racehorses is housed in stabling, the buildings and stalls where horses are accommodated.

clue.text: Books on TV are rewritten, as they go faster

indicators.note: something rewritten is put into new form, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Novels adapted for television get rewritten to speed up the pace.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forsyte Saga is John Galsworthy's sequence of novels, a hugely popular BBC television serial in 1967.
explanation.definitionFit: Galsworthy's linked novels about a wealthy family were famously serialised by the BBC, so they are books seen on television.

clue.text: Deceive the bank

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to mislead by pretending, as in poker
second meaning: a steep cliff or headland

explanation.surface: A fraudster cheating a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The bank is not a financial one but a steep slope of land.
explanation.definitionFit: To bluff is to mislead by a show of confidence, and a bluff is also a broad steep cliff or riverbank.

clue.text: The essence of a fashionable person

parts.note: in means in fashion
a being is a living person or creature

explanation.surface: What makes a trendy person tick.
explanation.definitionFit: Inbeing is an old philosophical word for inherent existence, the inner nature or quality of something.

clue.text: Look up description of bay

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse, so a red nag

explanation.surface: Consult a reference to find out what a bay is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look up' seems a single verb, but the definition is just 'Look' and 'up' turns the horse round. A gander is a look, as in 'take a gander'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a gander is informal for taking a look at something, borrowed from the goose stretching its neck.

clue.text: A fortress whose destruction caused strife

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so its letters can be rebuilt differently

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A castle was knocked down and fighting followed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wars of the Roses were the fifteenth-century English civil wars between the houses of Lancaster and York, a time when castles really were slighted.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth-century English civil wars between York and Lancaster were a long period of bitter strife.

clue.text: Turn one's back in a boxing-match with a grimace

parts.note: taken as written
a bout is a single contest in boxing
to pull a face is to grimace

explanation.surface: A boxer turns away from his opponent mid-fight, pulling a pained expression.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-face is a complete turnaround, originally the military drill command to swivel and face the opposite direction.

clue.text: City, but not the first of cities

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter of the city's name is dropped

parts.note: Durban is a port city in South Africa

explanation.surface: Someone names a city, then insists it is not the foremost of all cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like the definition, but it is the wordplay: DURBAN, the South African port, loses its D. The definition is the closing 'of cities'.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban is the adjective describing things belonging to towns and built-up areas, as opposed to rural countryside.

clue.text: Atrocious house, in ruins

indicators.note: a building in ruins has collapsed into a jumble, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful, derelict house that has fallen down.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous means shockingly wicked or evil, exactly as an atrocious crime is outrageously bad.

clue.text: In lyric, very loud old seventh note played in the wrong place

indicators.note: In tells us the following pieces are placed inside the poem

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
si is the older name for the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, now usually te

explanation.surface: A musician in a song hits a loud old note in the wrong place.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface hides a sporting definition: offside is a foul in football and rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: In football or rugby a player who is offside is positioned illegally ahead of the ball, so in the wrong place.

clue.text: Feel sorry about reactionary movement in sport

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to rue something is to regret or feel sorry about it

indicators.note: a reactionary wants to go backwards, so the word is turned round

parts.note: go is motion or movement

explanation.surface: Regret at a backward-looking trend in some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' is not a game here but the biological sense of an abnormal specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a sport is an organism showing abnormal variation from its type, and gardeners call such a deviant plant a rogue.

clue.text: A lot of plain speaking

parts.note: surface reading: a great deal of frank, blunt talk
setter's reading: plain spoken out loud is plane, so the clue means most of an aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: Say 'plain' and you hear the flying machine; a lot of a plane is its main body.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuselage is the main body of an aircraft, the largest part to which wings and tail are attached.

clue.text: Might oral, version, help in solving problems?

indicators.note: a version is a variant form, so the letters are arranged in another way

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Would a spoken version help someone work out their problems?
explanation.definitionFit: Before calculators, tables of logarithms were the standard aid for doing hard multiplication and division in arithmetic.

clue.text: Like 1984, gracious!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the novel Nineteen Eighty-Four was written ... Orwell
second meaning: a mild exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at how like the year 1984 things are.
explanation.walkthrough: 1984 is not the date but Orwell's novel, whose author used the pen name George Orwell.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel is a book written by its author George Orwell, and the same phrase is an old-fashioned exclamation like goodness gracious.

clue.text: Using fork to eat — not a bad notion

parts.note: a crotch is the fork where branches or legs divide

indicators.note: not, followed by the letter named, says that letter is left out

parts.note: taken as written, before losing a letter
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone suggests eating with a fork, which is not a bad idea at all.
explanation.walkthrough: EAT loses its A to leave ET. The surface 'not a bad notion' sounds like approval, but 'bad notion' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a perverse or eccentric whim, an odd fancy someone gets into their head.

clue.text: The service angle is unconventional…

parts.note: the Royal Air Force, one of the armed services
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: The armed forces' point of view is unorthodox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angle' looks like a noun, a viewpoint, but it is the verb for fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffish describes someone disreputable in an attractive way, careless of conventional standards of behaviour.

clue.text: Against interrupting poet's dressing

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
v, versus, means against

explanation.surface: An objection cutting into a poet's choice of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes inside GRAY. The surface suggests clothes, but the dressing is a sauce poured over food.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravy is a savoury sauce poured over meat, and a dressing is any sauce added to food.

clue.text: … and holds I gather some flavour

indicators.note: holds means the first word wraps around what follows

parts.note: taken as written, split around the contents
I see is a way of saying I understand or gather

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue: it contains, I understand, a certain taste.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry on from 19 down; the 'and' really is just the word and, opened up.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed, the seed of the anise plant, gives a liquorice-like taste used in sweets and drinks.

clue.text: One thousand and two hurt

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
a pair is two

explanation.surface: One thousand and two people were injured.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to damage or weaken something, so as a verb it can stand for hurt.

clue.text: Mute comforter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a device that deadens sound, as on a drum or exhaust
second meaning: a long warm woollen scarf

explanation.surface: Someone who consoles others in silence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sound-deadening device and a thick scarf wrapped round the neck, which British English calls a comforter.

clue.text: Girl in the cells

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a cluster of hermits' huts around a shared chapel

explanation.surface: A girl locked up in the police cells.
explanation.walkthrough: The cells are not a prison but a monastic settlement, a rare word also spelt lavra.
explanation.definitionFit: A laura was a group of separate dwellings for hermit monks in the early Eastern Church, and it is also a woman's name.

clue.text: Girl with artist's 10 fish

indicators.note: 10 points to the answer at 10 across, a turn to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Enid is a girl's name
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A girl joins an artist who is painting a still life of a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: ENID plus RA'S, read backwards. The cross-reference to 10 across is used as an instruction rather than as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardine is a small oily sea fish of the herring family, often sold packed in tins.

clue.text: Vale that's in the central area of Vaduz

indicators.note: in says one piece is put inside the other
the central area means only the middle letters of the place name are used

parts.note: the middle three letters of Vaduz, capital of Liechtenstein
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A valley found in the middle of Liechtenstein's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vale' looks like a valley, but it is the Latin word of farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Vale is Latin for farewell, and adieu is the French way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Tourist and he tigress be disturbed

indicators.note: to be disturbed is to be thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A wish that a tourist and a male tiger be left in peace, or perhaps upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A sightseer is someone visiting places of interest for pleasure, which is what a tourist does on holiday.

clue.text: Run over? Note the vehicle

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
the hearse is the vehicle that carries a coffin

explanation.surface: Someone run over, and a note on the vehicle that did it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run over' suggests a traffic accident, which the hearse seems to complete, but it means go through again.
explanation.definitionFit: To run over a speech or part is to go through it again for practice, which is to rehearse.

clue.text: Stick in glutinous mud, gets dirty

indicators.note: the letters are stuck inside the following words, embedded across their breaks

parts.note: the end of glutinous, all of mud and the start of gets

explanation.surface: Getting stuck in sticky mud leaves you filthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To smudge something is to smear it with a dirty mark, so smudge works as a verb meaning to make it dirty.
